stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the rotor to set the starting angle $\theta_0$, use the $I$ slider on the right to set the current, then press FIRE. The commutator keeps the torque driving in the same direction — the coil spins up as long as the current flows.
stages.concept: Laplace force on a current-carrying coil in a uniform field $\vec B$ produces a moment $M = N \cdot I \cdot S \cdot B \cdot \cos\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the angle between the coil plane and $\vec B$. The commutator flips $I$ at each half-turn so $M$ stays positive on average.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Sweep past all three target angles within the $1.5\,\text{s}$ simulation window. Higher $I$ = larger angular acceleration = wider sweep. The dashed arc previews the sweep for your current $I$ and $\theta_0$.
stages.concept: With the commutator, the average moment over one revolution is $M_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2 N I S B}{\pi}$. Starting from rest, the coil rotates as $\theta(t) = \theta_0 + \dfrac{M_{\text{avg}}}{2 J}\, t^{2}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview. A single target angle must be reached at exactly the deadline $t_{\text{tgt}}$ (tolerance $\pm 0.1\,\text{s}$ and $\pm 15^{\circ}$). Compute $I$ from $\theta_{\text{tgt}}$ and $t_{\text{tgt}}$ on paper, then fire. You have three shots — miss all three and the setup rotates.
stages.concept: Solve $\theta_{\text{tgt}} = \dfrac{M_{\text{avg}}}{2 J} t_{\text{tgt}}^{2}$ for $I$: $I = \dfrac{\pi\, J\, \theta_{\text{tgt}}}{N\, S\, B\, t_{\text{tgt}}^{2}}$. Doubling $I$ doubles the angular acceleration.

labels.tip2: use the preview arc to reach every target
labels.tip3: compute I from the target angle and time, then FIRE
labels.peek_tip_avg: Average moment with the commutator: M = 2·N·I·S·B / π. Constant on average.
labels.peek_tip_formula: From rest: θ(t) = M·t² / (2J). Solve for I given θ_tgt and t_tgt.
labels.peek_tip_scaling: Angular acceleration scales with I. Double I → same angle reached in 1/√2 of the time.

1.1: Drag the rotor to change the starting angle θ₀, then press FIRE.
1.2: The I slider on the right sets the coil current. Bigger I = faster spin-up.
1.3: Try a small I and a large I — notice how the coil sweeps a much wider angle for the same 1.5 s window.

2.1: The dashed arc is the sweep predicted for your current I and θ₀ over 1.5 s.
2.2: The farthest target sits at the largest angle — dial I up until the arc reaches it.
2.3: Starting angle θ₀ shifts the whole sweep. Adjust it to bracket the closest target too.

3.1: Read θ_tgt and t_tgt. Use θ = M·t² / (2J) with M = 2NISB/π to solve for I.
3.2: I = π·J·θ_tgt / (N·S·B·t_tgt²). Values: J = 10⁻³ kg·m², N = 100, S = 5·10⁻⁴ m², B = 0.15 T.
3.3: Round I to the slider step (0.1 A) — the ±15° tolerance absorbs the rounding.
